A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MetamerGen work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, references, and appendices A.1–A.10 are readable and support comparison despite reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original COCO image-generation evaluations, human same-different experiments, feature-response analyses, and computational and behavioral ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains original model evaluations and human-study outcomes, including metamer rates, feature correlations, conditioning-stream ablations, and the DINOv2–CLIP comparison.

M1.justification: The dual-stream DINOv2 conditioning, Perceiver resamplers, Stable Diffusion 1.5 adapters, trainable components, and DDIM/CFG++ inference remain unchanged. The added distinction between training-time random fixations and experiment-dependent inference clarifies an existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use COCO training images, COCO-10k-test evaluation, and 300 Visual Genome images sourced from YFCC100M for the same behavioral tasks. No new dataset, population type, or test scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: The SD-1.5 text-to-image baseline in Figure 2 and CLIP encoder comparison in Appendix A.10 are retained. Random-fixation comparisons and foveal-only, peripheral-only, and original-image controls also remain.

E3.justification: v1 Section 5.2 describes 12 participants as additionally seeing random-fixation generations; v3 Section 4.2 describes 12 other participants in that condition. This revises the reported participant allocation without establishing that experiments were rerun. Fixation counts, presentation timings, training settings, and evaluation metrics are retained.

E4.justification: Figure 3 replaces the non-metamer examples illustrating generations rejected by participants, revising the qualitative case evidence. The quantitative conditioning, blur, token-count, encoder, regression, and feature analyses are retained, including those moved within the appendices.

E5.justification: The correlation and significance reporting, plotted error bars, and regression procedures are unchanged. No new seed, repeated-run, or uncertainty-estimation procedure is documented; the newly stated Gabor significance outcome is a result-reporting change.

E6.justification: v3 Appendix A.5.1 newly states that the 90° Gabor-filter effect was not significant, and Figure 3 supplies replacement qualitative results. The numerical plots and reported headline rates remain unchanged, including 29.4% versus 27.7% and the conditioning-ablation rates of 54.5%, 45.8%, and 8.4%.

T1.justification: The attention, conditioning, and Perceiver equations (1–7) retain their mathematical content. Changes combine notation or adjust formatting; neither version adds formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contribution claims are retained. However, v3 frames the benefit of additional fixations as an expectation in the introduction and adds a prospective claim about assistive technologies in the discussion, modestly changing claim qualification and scope.

C2.justification: v1 explains DreamSim's advantage through nonlinguistic mid-to-high-level features; v3 instead emphasizes its training on human similarity judgments. v3 also emphasizes the clearer depth effect relative to proto-object segmentation and locates the DreamSim condition difference at high distances. The generation-artifact limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-page link, explicitly states 300 experimental trials, and documents the chin rest, head restraint, and use of default fixation-detection algorithms in subsequent analyses. These are additional disclosures; the existing hardware, optimizer, training budget, preprocessing, and output-resolution details are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Rensink (2000), The dynamic representation of scenes, to support its proto-object discussion. The broader literature coverage and positioning relative to diffusion adapters, visual encoders, and previous metamer research remain stable.

P1.justification: Much of the introduction, behavioral paradigm, results, and discussion is rewritten. v3 reorders the preliminaries, incorporates image-generation quality as Section 3.4, reorganizes appendix material, and adds acknowledgments. This is an extensive narrative and structural revision despite largely stable scientific content.

P2.justification: v3 enlarges Figures 1, 4, and 5, reduces Figure 15, replaces Figure 3's non-metamer montage, revises judgment labels and captions, and swaps the order of the Gabor and object-detection figures. The underlying quantitative displays retain their structure and content.

improvement.justification: The clearer results roadmap, reorganized appendices, larger key figures, and added behavioral setup details make the existing evidence easier to assess. Explicitly reporting the 90° Gabor null result improves completeness. These are useful but limited gains: the quantitative validation is retained, and the new assistive-technology forecast remains speculative.
